transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Rivera (Redwood CSM), Lena Morris (Vertex Head of ML), Rahul Singh (Platform Eng), Jamal Ortiz (Security), Hannah Lee (Data Eng), Tom Baker (Dev Lead)

Summary: quick check-in on Private VPC pilot; focused on networking issues (peering, NAT), routing to private inference nodes, and a requested runtime upgrade for better NVLink behavior. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: network connectivity, routing / private endpoints, runtime upgrade, perf regression observed on long context, security questions (audit logs / KMS), pilot timeline

Transcript:
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, joining with Maya and Diego. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Lena: hey Alex, doing well thanks, a few people dialed in late but we're good.
00:12 Maya: quick goal for today, I want to confirm the networking checklist, review the perf numbers from last run, and go over the upgrade plan for the runtime we talked about.
00:21 Rahul: packed agenda, yeah we hit a weird outage yesterday where requests to the private endpoints timed out intermittently. we captured some tcp dumps.
00:30 Maya: ok can you remind me if those requests went via the transit gateway or direct VPC peering?
00:36 Rahul: they were through the TGW, we have a hub-and-spoke. sometimes the TGW route table got stuck without the route to the dedicated subnets, so things fell back to the NAT and then timed out or got rate limited.
00:50 Alex: got it. that's consistent with the traceroutes we asked for, we saw a couple of asymmetric paths—one hop was hitting the firewall cluster that trims idle connections.
00:59 Jamal: yeah that firewall is managed by our infra team. we were seeing idle tcp timeouts at 30s which clashes with Redwood's long-lived streaming connections.
01:09 Maya: right, Redwood streaming keeps an idle window on client socket a bit longer, we recommend extending the firewall idle timeout to 300s or configuring a keepalive from the client.
01:19 Tom: quick Q, is there a requirement for specific ports outbound? we have a restrictive egress policy.
01:24 Maya: yes, minimal list: 443 outbound to the control plane endpoints, and a set of internal ports for the private runtime communication - primarily 9000-9010 TCP for inference and 16000-16010 for redis-ish KV cache. i'll send a compact list after the call.
01:38 Rahul: that 16000-16010, we're using an internal redis cluster; is that KV cache the same or are you recommending a separate service?
01:44 Maya: good question. currently the pilot uses the in-runtime KV-ish cache over that port range; for production you can either co-locate with your redis or use the Redwood-managed KV over a peered private endpoint. both patterns are supported.
01:59 Lena: on perf numbers, Hannah sent the run where tokens/sec dropped by ~15% at sequence len 2k, any clues?
02:07 Maya: yes we looked at logs; two things. first, the model run landed on a host with mixed GPU topology and no NVLink peer access; second, the kernel selection fell back to a conservative path because of a mismatch in the compiled kernels after a recent micro-upgrade.
02:22 Alex: that compiles to slower matmul and extra memcpy, so latency and throughput both took a hit. we should get you a runtime that has the new kernel selection heuristics and explicit NVLink-aware placement.
02:33 Hannah: is that the build you mentioned last week, the 1.8.2-rc?
02:38 Maya: yes exactly, 1.8.2-rc includes the NVLink affinity and a fix for the large context KV flush. we've validated on our internal bench but not on your cluster yet.
02:48 Lena: what's the risk of flipping that build in the pilot, do we need to reprovision nodes?
02:54 Maya: no reprovision required - it's a rolling agent + runtime package update. but we do recommend draining the node before the upgrade to avoid in-flight requests hitting an older code path.
03:07 Rahul: ok we can schedule a maintenance window. can the upgrade be reverted quickly?
03:11 Maya: yes, we keep the previous runtime and can rollback within ~10-15 minutes per node if needed.
03:18 Tom: earlier Kafka backlog caused higher latencies, is there any interaction with batching?
03:22 Maya: batching is adaptive; if message broker backpressure spikes we will see larger batches which increase tail latency. part of the tuning is batch size and max wait; we'll share recommended settings per workload.
03:33 Rahul: also noticed auth failures from the control plane yesterday, any root cause?
03:37 Diego: Diego here - I checked the logs, the token issuer was rotating keys and some long-lived sessions with older tokens hit a 401 until they re-authenticated. we've changed the rotation window and added graceful rollover.
03:50 Jamal: on security, can you confirm that audit logs for inference requests are delivered to our S3 bucket? we need that for the compliance team.
03:57 Alex: yes, we can forward audit logs to your S3 and we support encryption with your KMS key; we'll add that to the checklist.
04:05 Jamal: and is access to the admin console locked down via SAML only?
04:09 Diego: we support SAML/SSO and can enforce IP allowlists for the console management plane; we'll capture the required artifacts for your audit.
04:19 Lena: about the intermittent timeouts - Rahul uploaded the tcpdump; it shows a couple of RSTs when the connection hits the firewall. we can try increasing idle timeouts but is there anything on Redwood's side that keeps connections open unnecessarily?
04:33 Maya: we do keep streaming connections open for long-running completions; if firewall kills them we lose the socket and have to reconnect which shows up to clients as a timeout. keepalives or firewall tune is the fix.
04:45 Alex: operationally, we also recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated requests to reduce connection churn and token cost, that might reduce the pressure.
04:55 Hannah: on metrics, we saw memory climb on the node during longer contexts. any ideas?
04:59 Maya: can you share the heap/profile? the runtime uses an async prefetch for the KV cache; if key eviction isn't tuned for long contexts you can see memory spikes. there's a flag to lower the prefetch window.
05:12 Hannah: ok I'll pull the memory profile and post it.
05:16 Tom: question re network path - do you recommend colocating the Redis KV in the same subnet as the inference nodes?
05:22 Maya: yes, co-location reduces latency; if you can't, then peered private endpoints with ENI attachments work fine but ensure MTU and active path is consistent.
05:31 Rahul: i wanted to surface one more thing: the autoscale policy we applied didn't trigger new nodes when we saw a sustained qps spike. we set CPU threshold but it seems GPU metrics aren't wired.
05:41 Alex: we do recommend using the Redwood GPU worker metric or the inference queue latency metric for autoscaling rather than host CPU. Maya can help map the correct metric to your cloud autoscaler.
05:51 Maya: i'll send the mapping chart after the call. for now, use queue_latency > 200ms sustained as a heuristic.
05:58 Lena: any blockers for us to run the upgrade this week?
06:01 Maya: not from our side. primary blocker is the firewall idle timeout change and a short maintenance window to drain nodes. also we need the traceroute that shows the transit gateway path which Rahul already uploaded.
06:12 Rahul: I'll coordinate with infra to open the change request and we'll aim for 2026-08-25 02:00 UTC maintenance window.
06:19 Diego: i'll be standing by for the upgrade and will coordinate rollback plan.
06:23 Alex: great. one more item - we noticed a small divergence in log formats which makes parsing harder for your SIEM. we'll enable a compatibility mode that outputs the fields in the same order as your current schema.
06:36 Jamal: perfect. also can you add the KMS key policy template to the security doc?
06:40 Diego: yes i'll attach the template and a short how-to.
06:44 Maya: quick note on performance tests - we'd like to run a short benchmark post-upgrade with synthetic 2k and 4k sequences to validate tokens/sec. can we get test credentials?
06:55 Lena: yes, we'll create a test role with minimal perms. Rahul and Hannah will create creds and add to the vault.
07:03 Alex: ok to recap next steps: Redwood sends network port list and upgrade build; Vertex runs the egress/keepalive test and schedules the maintenance window for 2026-08-25; SE will run the post-upgrade benchmark and share numbers; security items (KMS template, audit log config) delivered by Diego.
07:24 Lena: that matches our notes. last Q from me: what's the expected perf delta after the NVLink-aware placement?
07:31 Maya: we expect 10-20% improvement for long-context runs where NVLink reduces cross-device memcpy; exact numbers will depend on the node topology.
07:41 Tom: ok thanks everyone.
07:44 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread and i'll drop the network diagram today.
07:48 Diego: thanks, bye.
07:50 Meeting end
